(a) Conduct exploratory data analysis (EDA) and apply necessary pre-processing steps to prepare the data for PCA and clustering, (7 marks) How many eigenvectors are needed to retain 90% of the variance of the original data? (3 marks) and Display the top 5 eigenvalues and their corresponding eigenvectors. (4 marks) Note: Don't consider target column fetal_health in PCA and clustering.

# Load Dataset
df = pd.read_csv('/content/fetal_health.csv')

# ==================== EDA ====================

print("================ Dataset Head ================")
print(df.head())

print("\n================ Dataset Shape ================")
print(df.shape)

print("\n================ Dataset Information ================")
df.info()

print("\n================ Null Values Count ================")
print(df.isna().sum())

print("\n================ Duplicate Rows ================")
print(df.duplicated().sum())

print("\n================ Unique Values Count ================")
print(df.nunique())

# Remove Duplicate Rows
df = df.drop_duplicates()

print("\nShape after removing duplicates:", df.shape)

# Boxplot (excluding target column)
plt.figure(figsize=(20, 10))
sns.boxplot(data=df.drop(columns=['fetal_health']))
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.title("Feature Distribution")
plt.show()

# Correlation Heatmap (excluding target column)
plt.figure(figsize=(18, 10))
sns.heatmap(df.drop(columns=['fetal_health']).corr(),
            annot=True, cmap='coolwarm')
plt.title("Correlation Matrix")
plt.show()

# ==================== PREPROCESSING ====================

# Exclude target column
X = df.drop('fetal_health', axis=1)

# Handle Missing Values
imputer = SimpleImputer(strategy='median')
X_imputed = imputer.fit_transform(X)

# Standardization
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_imputed)

standardized = pd.DataFrame(X_scaled, columns=X.columns)

print("\n================ Standardized Data ================")
print(standardized.head())

# ==================== PCA ====================

pca = PCA()
X_pca = pca.fit_transform(X_scaled)

# Calculate Cumulative Explained Variance
cumulative_variance = np.cumsum(pca.explained_variance_ratio_)

# Find Components Required for 90% Variance
n_components = np.argmax(cumulative_variance >= 0.90) + 1

print("\nNumber of eigenvectors needed to retain 90% variance:",
      n_components)

print("Variance Retained:",
      cumulative_variance[n_components - 1] * 100, "%")

# Plot Cumulative Explained Variance
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(range(1, len(cumulative_variance) + 1),
         cumulative_variance, marker='o')

plt.axhline(y=0.90, color='red', linestyle='--')
plt.axvline(x=n_components, color='green', linestyle='--')

plt.xlabel("Number of Components")
plt.ylabel("Cumulative Explained Variance")
plt.title("Cumulative Explained Variance vs Number of Components")
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

# ==================== TOP 5 EIGENVALUES AND EIGENVECTORS ====================

eigenvalues = pca.explained_variance_[:5]
eigenvectors = pca.components_[:5]

print("\n================ Top 5 Eigenvalues ================")
print(eigenvalues)

print("\n================ Top 5 Eigenvectors ================")

eigenvectors_df = pd.DataFrame(
    eigenvectors,
    columns=X.columns,
    index=['PC1', 'PC2', 'PC3', 'PC4', 'PC5']
)

print(eigenvectors_df)

# Variance Explained by Top 5 Components
total_variance = pca.explained_variance_ratio_[:5].sum()

print("\nVariance Explained by Top 5 Components:")
print(total_variance * 100, "%")

  1. The dataset contains 2,126 records and 22 columns, with no missing values. A total of 13 duplicate records were identified and removed.
  2. Boxplots help identify outliers, while the correlation heatmap shows relationships and dependencies among the numerical features.
  3. The target column fetal_health was excluded, and the remaining 21 features were standardized using StandardScaler.
  4. PCA was applied to reduce dimensionality. The minimum number of principal components required to retain 90% of the variance was identified.
  5. Eigenvalues indicate the variance captured by each principal component, while eigenvectors represent the contribution of the original features to the principal components.

(b) Identify the ideal number of K-means clusters based on principal components retaining 90% explained variance, and visualize the results with the SilhouetteVisualizer..

In [18]:
k_values = range(2, 11)
silhouette_scores = {}
fig,axes = plt.subplots(2,5,figsize=(20,10))
for ax,k in zip(axes.flatten(),k_values):
    model  = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42, n_init=10)
    visualizer = SilhouetteVisualizer(model, colors='yellowbrick', ax=ax)
    visualizer.fit(X_pca)
    silhouette_scores[k] = visualizer.silhouette_score_
    ax.set_title(f'K={k}, score={visualizer.silhouette_score_:.3f}')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
  1. Silhouette scores were calculated for different cluster values (K = 2 to 10) to identify the optimal number of clusters.
  2. K = 2 gives the highest silhouette score of 0.200, indicating it is the best clustering choice among the tested values.
  3. As the number of clusters increases, the silhouette score generally decreases, indicating weaker cluster separation.
  4. Negative silhouette values in some clusters indicate overlapping clusters and possible incorrect assignments of data points.
  5. Overall, K = 2 is the optimal choice among the tested values. However, the low silhouette score suggests that the clusters are not very well separated.

(c) Generate dendrograms for the top 20 clusters using five different linkage methods. Use principal components explaining 90% of the variance, compute the cophenetic correlation coefficient for each method, and print the results for comparison.

In [26]:
methods = ['single','complete','average','centroid','ward']
distances = pdist(X_pca, metric='euclidean')
ccc_results = []
plt.figure(figsize=(20,18))

for i,method in enumerate(methods):
  Z = linkage(distances, method=method)
  c, coph_dists = cophenet(Z, distances)
  ccc_results.append({'Linkage Method': method, 'Cophenetic Correlation Coefficient': c})

  # Plot dendrogram
  plt.subplot(3, 2, i + 1)
  dendrogram(Z,truncate_mode='lastp',p=20,leaf_rotation=90,leaf_font_size=10)
  plt.title(f'{method.capitalize()} Linkage (CCC={c:.4f})')
  plt.xlabel('Clusters')
  plt.ylabel('Distance')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Print CCC comparison
ccc_df = pd.DataFrame(ccc_results)

print("\n========== COPHENETIC CORRELATION COMPARISON ==========")
print(ccc_df)

# Identify best linkage method
best_method = ccc_df.loc[
    ccc_df['Cophenetic Correlation Coefficient'].idxmax()
]

print("\nBest Linkage Method:", best_method['Linkage Method'])
print("Highest CCC:", best_method['Cophenetic Correlation Coefficient'])

(d) Partition the data into three clusters and evaluate the quality of each cluster by ranking them based on their within-cluster sum of squares (WCSS). Use PCA-transformed data that retains 90% of the variance.

In [22]:
kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=3, random_state=42, n_init = 10)
clusters = kmeans.fit_predict(X_pca)
wcss = []
for i in range(3):
  cluster_points = X_pca[clusters == i]
  centroid = kmeans.cluster_centers_[i]
  cluster_wcss = np.sum((cluster_points - centroid) ** 2)
  wcss.append(cluster_wcss)

wcss_df = pd.DataFrame({'cluster':['0','1','2'], 'WCSS':wcss})
wcss_df.sort_values(by='WCSS', ascending=False, inplace=True)

print(wcss_df)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 10))

plt.scatter(X_pca[:, 0], X_pca[:, 1],
            c=clusters, cmap='Set2', s=18)

plt.xlabel("PC1")
plt.ylabel("PC2")
plt.title("K-Means Clustering with PCA (3 Clusters)")
plt.show()

models = {"K Means": KMeans(n_clusters =  2, random_state = 42, n_init= 20),
          "Agglomorative": AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters = 2)}

results = []

for name, model in models.items():
  labels = model.fit_predict(X_scaled)
  results.append({
      "Model": name, "Silhouette Score": silhouette_score(X_scaled,labels),
      "Calinski Harabasz Score": calinski_harabasz_score(X_scaled,labels),
      "Davies Bouldin Score": davies_bouldin_score(X_scaled,labels)
  })
comparision = pd.DataFrame(results).set_index("Model")
display(comparision)

# Visualize comparison
comparision.plot(kind="bar", figsize=(12, 5))

plt.title("K-Means vs Agglomerative Clustering")
plt.ylabel("Score")
plt.xticks(rotation=0)

3 (a)
Read the 'bread_basket.csv' file, perform required pre-processing, Build the Apriori ML model with minimum support 10% and print values of Lift greater than 2.

Use the dataset: bread_basket.csv

In [31]:
#Loading dataset

basket = pd.read_csv('/content/bread_basket.csv')
basket.head()

transactions = basket.apply(
    lambda row:[str(x).strip() for x in row.dropna() if str(x).strip()],axis=1).tolist()

#converting transaction into boolean matrix
encoder = TransactionEncoder()
encoded_data = encoder.fit(transactions).transform(transactions)

basket_matrix = pd.DataFrame(encoded_data, columns=encoder.columns_)

# Display dataset information
print("Total transaction",len(transactions))
print("unique items", basket_matrix.shape[1])

#Apply apriori algorithem with correct relative support of 10%
frequent_items = apriori(basket_matrix, min_support = 0.10, use_colnames = True)

#generate association rule with lift >2
rules = association_rules(frequent_items, metric = "lift", min_threshold = 2.0)
rule_columns =  ["antecedents", "consequents", "support", "confidence", "lift"]
display(rules[

# Step 1: Install and import libraries
!pip install scikit-surprise

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from surprise import Dataset, Reader, SVD
from surprise.model_selection import cross_validate

# Step 2: Load dataset
ratings = pd.read_csv('/content/Musical_Instruments_ratings.csv')

# Step 3: Filter active users and popular items
user_counts = ratings['UserID'].value_counts()
item_counts = ratings['ItemID'].value_counts()

active_users = user_counts[user_counts >= 15].index
popular_items = item_counts[item_counts >= 20].index

ratings_model = ratings[
    ratings['UserID'].isin(active_users) &
    ratings['ItemID'].isin(popular_items)
].copy()

print("Filtered Dataset Shape:", ratings_model.shape)

# Step 4: Prepare data for recommendation model
reader = Reader(rating_scale=(1, 5))

data = Dataset.load_from_df(
    ratings_model[['UserID', 'ItemID', 'Rating']],
    reader
)

# Step 5: Build SVD collaborative filtering model
model = SVD(n_factors=16, n_epochs=8, random_state=42)

# Step 6: Perform 3-fold cross-validation
results = cross_validate(
    model, data, measures=['RMSE'], cv=3, verbose=True
)

print("\nMean 3-Fold RMSE:", round(results['test_rmse'].mean(), 4))

# Step 7: Train model on complete filtered dataset
trainset = data.build_full_trainset()
model.fit(trainset)

# Step 8: Recommend top 5 items to a specific user
user_id = ratings_model['UserID'].iloc[0]

rated_items = ratings_model[
    ratings_model['UserID'] == user_id
]['ItemID'].tolist()

unrated_items = [
    item for item in ratings_model['ItemID'].unique()
    if item not in rated_items
]

predictions = [
    (item, model.predict(user_id, item).est)
    for item in unrated_items
]

top_5 = sorted(
    predictions, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True
)[:5]
